newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, focus on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, focus on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate late trading on Thursday, with operators seen focusing on Friday liquidity, dealers said.
"The market still seems to be nervous over Friday liquidity conditions," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said operators were wary about possible carry-forward effects of tight conditions from previous Fridays although the impact was seen diminishing last Friday.
However, the fears and the fact that Friday was the last day to improve banks' positions ahead of the next liquidity report on October 15 caused short-dated swaps to rise, he said.
"It's a good chance to arbitrage," the dealer said.
Dealers said focus was on tom/next swap rate which rose to 3.50/3.70 points from 2.75/3.0 points at the opening.
Overnight swap closed at 0.55/0.65 points.

Dealers said rupiah supply in the money market was not that tight but the market was driven up mainly by rising swap rates. "Major players are still short in the forward market. They are taking short-dated swaps to cover positions. Friday would be the last chance to improve off-balance sheet positions," one said.
But the Japanese bank dealer said interbank rates may ease on Friday if major players could square off on Thursday.
Overnight money fell to 10.0 percent from 14.0/15.0 percent in the morning, one local bank dealer said.
"It seems people here are speculating for a tight Friday. I just got hit (on tom/next swap) all the way up," he said, adding that both local and offshore players were present.
The Japanese bank dealer said some operators seemed to be caught by the off-balance sheet limitations which forced them to take up swaps instead of cheaper rates in the money market.
Tom/next rupiah was quoted at 16.5 percent, compared with the equivalent of tom/next swap at around 18.76 percent.
Dealers said expensive short-dated swap rates continued to cause some adjustments in longer-term swap premiums.
One-month swap edged up to 19.50/20.00 from 18.5/19.5, two to 36.50/37.50 from 35.0/36.5, three to 53.50/54.50 from 53.0/55.0 and six to 103.0/104.5 from 102.5/104.5 points.
Dealers said offshore players were still speculating for a band widening but the view was not shared by local operators as the central bank had just widened its band last September.
The Japanese bank dealer said offshore pressure to test the central bank's band seemed to have eased in the afternoon.

"Dollar offers were immediately off from brokers' boxes after knowing the central bank has raised the fixing by one point. This may indicate that offshore players didn't want to proceed with the challenge for today," the dealer said.
Offshore operators started testing the band late on Wednesday, raising the rupiah out of the central bank's ceiling after the official squaring time at 0900 GMT.
However, the rupiah had returned to within the parameters of the central bank intervention band this morning. State bank dealers said the central bank did not intervene on Wednesday.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,320.5/20.60 at 0945 GMT against an opening of 2,320.50/21.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,317.00/17.35 and 2,316.25/16.75, respectively.
One U.S. bank dealer said earlier offshore players were trying to create reasons to sell dollars and also to challenge the central bank, Bank Indonesia.
One currency dealer in Singapore said offshore players were heavily short on dollars.
"I don't think Bank Indonesia would give in to offshore pressure," the U.S. bank dealer said.
"I don't think the central bank would widen its band again at present," one economist attached to a state bank said.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,320/2,512 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,320/2,368 on Thursday.
-- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364.
